newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian blue chips up, rest of market down.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian blue chips up, rest of market down.

text.p: Investors snapped up blue chips at Lithuania's stock exchange on Wednesday, as several key shares pushed up the official list but the broader group-A index sagged.
The official list jumped 17.72 points to 978.58 points while group-A shares declined by 7.01 points to 1853.16 points.
"Blue chips are expected to gain again tomorrow," said one broker.
Central market turnover slipped to 527,000 litas from 622,000 litas.
Dealers said that investors were still seeking the security of the official list companies, with their proven track records and transparancy.
Official list lead Vilniaus Bank advanced to 249 litas from 245 litas on central market turnover of 71,000 litas as the market responded to its audited interim results.
Vilniaus Bank said on Tuesday its audited profit for the first half of 1997 was 21.7 million litas versus 11.7 million litas in the same period last year.
Vilniaus Bank also saw bloc trades worth 100,000 litas at 250 litas.
Hermis Bank advanced to 229 from 221 in central market turnover of 117,000 litas.
Rokishkis Cheese, one of three corporate blue chips on the official list, crept up to 44 litas from 42.95 litas on central market turnover of 148,000 litas.

Rokishkis said this month its profits for the first six months of 1997 rose to 9.5 million litas from 1.25 million litas in the same period last year, but its shares have yet to show clear signs of a steady advance.
